summary: Handrio Nurhan is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed a BA at Soka University of America (2011-2015), an MA at Texas Tech University (2016-2018), and PhD studies at Boston University in 2018.
Hank Glassman works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He held posts at Haverford College, where he was attested in 2009 and as a faculty member in 2019.

Hanna Havnevik specializes in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She held posts at the University of Oslo, serving as Professor (attested 2006-2008) and later as Professor Emerita (attested 2026).

Hanna Wałkówska was an Indologist who studied at the University of Breslau under Ludwik Skurzak (~1946-1950). She subsequently held an academic post at the University of Breslau from circa 1950 to 1991.

Hannah Gould specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. Educated at the University of Melbourne and University of Oxford, she held posts at Monash University, St Vincent's Hospital Melbourne, and as Lecturer in Buddhist Studies at Melbourne (2024).

Hannes Sköld was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Gothenburg (~1904-1907) and Lund University (~1907-1916). He served at Lund University as Docent of Slavonic Languages (1920) and Comparative IE Linguistics (1926).

Hanns Oertel was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at Yale under William Dwight Whitney (~1888-1890). He held posts at Yale (1891-1917), Marburg (1922-1925), and Munich (1925-1935), among other appointments.

Hanns-Peter Schmidt was a scholar of Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After completing his PhD at Hamburg under Ludwig Alsdorf (~1951-1957), he served at Deccan College, Dr. Hari Singh Gour University, Tübingen, and UCLA (1965-2000).

Hans Adolf Dietrich Hartmann was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Marburg, Berlin (PhD 1930-1933), and Dublin. He held posts as PD in Berlin (1941) and Göttingen (1948), and was Professor at Hamburg (1953-1978).

Hans Conon von der Gabelentz worked in linguistics, Sinology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the universities of Leipzig and Göttingen between 1825 and 1828, and founded the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft.
Hans Delbrück was a historian who studied at the University of Bonn (~1869-1873). He held posts at Frederick William University Berlin (1885) and the Humboldt University of Berlin (~1885-1921).

Hans E. Kauffmann was a scholar of history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Vienna under Robert von Heine-Geldern (~1928-1934) and earned his PhD from the University of Zurich (~1930-1934).

Hans Frederik Hendriksen was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Copenhagen and across Europe. He was Professor at Uppsala University (1947-1951) and Professor of Indian-Eastern philology at Copenhagen (1951-1983).

Hans Haas worked in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Erlangen-Nuremberg, he held posts at the German Theological High School (1898), University of Tokyo (~1904-1909), Jena (1913), and Leipzig (1915).

Hans Harder is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Hamburg, Heidelberg, and Halle-Wittenberg (PhD under Rahul Peter Das, Habilitation), serving as Assistent at Halle-Wittenberg (1995-2007) and on editorial boards at Heidelberg and Gonda Indological Studies.
Hans Hartog was an Indology scholar who studied at Tübingen, Bethel, and Munich before earning his PhD at the University of Marburg under Friedrich Heiler (~1936-1939).

Hans Heinrich Schaeder worked in Iranian studies and religious studies. After earning a PhD at Breslau (~1915-1920), he held professorships at Königsberg (1926), Leipzig (1930-1931), Humboldt University of Berlin (1931-1944), and Göttingen (1946-1957).

Hans Henrich Hock is a linguist and Indologist who completed graduate studies at Northwestern and Yale (under Warren Crawford Cowgill). He served as Professor of Linguistics and Sanskrit at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~1967-2007).

Hans Jensen Jørgensen was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Marburg, Munich, and Kiel, earning his PhD under Emil Sieg in 1911. He worked as a scientific assistant at the Ethnological Museum of Berlin (1912-1919).
Hans Josef Nolte was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He completed a PhD at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1892-1894) and served as Director of Gymnasium Papenburg from 1904 to 1916.
